heading: Deck maths: theory behind deck_math.py and deck_optimize.py
text: Card choices from `card_usage.py` are **statistics** (what tournament lists play). The tools below add **calculation**: exact odds, simulated consistency, and a search for better flex slots. They never edit a deck.
source: standard probability theory; game numbers from data/format.json (Comprehensive Rules 1.10.0)

heading: 1. Hypergeometric distribution (exact)
text: Drawing `n` cards without replacement from a deck of `N` that holds `K` hits: P(X = x) = C(K, x) * C(N - K, n - x) / C(N, n) P(X >= k) = sum over x = k .. min(K, n) of P(X = x) Example: 4 copies in 50 cards, 5-card opening hand: P(at least 1) = 1 - C(46,5)/C(50,5) = 35.4%. Redraw (6-2-1-6): the first hand goes to the bottom and the new hand comes from the other 45 cards, so P(open with at least 1 after an optional redraw) = p1 + (1 - p1) * p2, with p2 computed on 45 cards (`deck_stats.py`).
source: standard probability theory; game numbers from data/format.json (Comprehensive Rules 1.10.0)

heading: 2. Multivariate hypergeometric (exact joint odds)
text: For disjoint groups with K_1..K_m copies and minimums a_1..a_m, R = N - sum(K_i) other cards: P(X_i >= a_i for all i) = sum over x_i >= a_i, sum(x_i) <= n of [ prod C(K_i, x_i) ] * C(R, n - sum x_i) / C(N, n) Use: "a Unit **and** a Pilot that links to it both seen by turn 3" (`deck_math.py --joint A:1,B:1 --by 3`). Two independent 1-in-4 odds multiplied together are wrong here, because the groups compete for the same draws.
source: standard probability theory; game numbers from data/format.json (Comprehensive Rules 1.10.0)

heading: 3. Level and cards seen per turn (deterministic)
text: - Level on your turn t = min(t, 10) + 1 if you go second (EX Resource, 6-2-4). The resource deck adds exactly one Resource per turn (7-4-1), so level is not random. Only the main-deck draws are random. - Cards seen by your main phase on turn t = 5 + t (one draw per turn, 7-3). - The project's rules notes list no turn-1 draw skip for player one. `--skip-first-draw` exists in case the official document says otherwise. **Verify against the Comprehensive Rules before relying on turn-1 numbers.** - A card is castable on turn t when Lv <= level and cost <= active Resources (2-9-1, 2-10-1).
source: standard probability theory; game numbers from data/format.json (Comprehensive Rules 1.10.0)

heading: 4. Monte Carlo goldfish (simulated)
text: "Goldfish" means playing with no opponent. Each game shuffles the deck, applies the redraw policy (redraw if no Unit of Lv <= `--keep-lv`), then each turn: draw, add a Resource, and greedily play the most expensive castable Units / Pilots / Bases first (Pilots pair onto a Unit, preferring a link). The EX Resource is removed once it is spent. Per turn it measures: played anything, dead turn (nothing castable), resources spent / available, Units on the field, link formed so far.
source: standard probability theory; game numbers from data/format.json (Comprehensive Rules 1.10.0)

heading: Confidence intervals
text: - Rates use the **Wilson score interval** (accurate near 0% and 100%, unlike p +/- 1.96 sqrt(p(1-p)/n)): centre = (p + z^2/2n) / (1 + z^2/n) half = z * sqrt(p(1-p)/n + z^2/4n^2) / (1 + z^2/n), z = 1.96 - Means use mean +/- 1.96 * sd / sqrt(n). - A fixed seed makes every run repeatable; change the seed to check that a result is not luck of one seed.
source: standard probability theory; game numbers from data/format.json (Comprehensive Rules 1.10.0)

heading: 5. Meta-weighted expected match win (from your log)
text: - Game win rate per opposing archetype, smoothed with a **Beta(2,2) prior**: p = (wins + 2) / (games + 4). With 0 games p = 50%; with 3-0 p = 71%, not 100%. Small samples cannot claim certainty. - Best-of-3 match win from a game win rate p (games independent): P = p^2 + 2 p^2 (1 - p) = **p^2 (3 - 2p)**. p = 0.60 gives 64.8%: best-of-3 magnifies an edge. - Expected match win against the field = sum over archetypes of share_a * P(p_a), shares from tournament decklists. - Unlogged archetypes count as 50%. The figure is only as good as your log.
source: standard probability theory; game numbers from data/format.json (Comprehensive Rules 1.10.0)

heading: 6. Optimization (deck_optimize.py)
text: Score per simulated game: score = w_curve * curve + w_spend * spend + w_link * link + w_usage * usage - curve = fraction of turns 1..T where you played something - spend = resources spent / resources available (mana efficiency) - link = 1 if a link formed on any turn up to `--link-turn` (default: the last simulated turn, so late links such as a Lv6 Unit's are counted) - Pilots that link to a locked Unit are locked with it, because the goldfish under-values them - usage = average meta share of the cards in the deck. This is a Bayesian-style prior: it pulls the search towards cards that tournament lists already play, so the maths refines the statistics instead of ignoring them. **Search** is a hill-climb over flex slots: try every legal `-N out / +N in` (N = 1 or 2), keep the best. It repeats up to `--max-swaps` times. Every candidate passes `deck_check.py` rules. **Common random numbers**: every candidate is scored on the same shuffles, so a difference between two lists comes from the cards, not from different luck. The final list is re-checked on fresh shuffles (another seed) with a **paired** interval on the per-game difference. If that interval includes 0, the gain is noise. **Sensitivity**: the score lost when one copy of a card is replaced by a blank card. This is the value of that copy in the model. The lowest rows are the weakest slots in the model, not necessarily in the real game.
source: standard probability theory; game numbers from data/format.json (Comprehensive Rules 1.10.0)

heading: 7. Limits (say these when presenting results)
text: - No opponent, no interaction, no card effects (draw, search and removal are invisible). Commands are never cast, so they are locked by default. - The goldfish favours cheap cards: a list of only low-cost Units scores well and loses real games. The usage weight and locked core cards are the guard against that. - Matchup strength is not modelled. It comes only from logged games (section 5). - Every proposed swap goes to the Deck Analyst: check live text (`fetch_card.py`) and the meta before proposing it, then Before/After and "yes" before TCG Lead edits the deck.
source: standard probability theory; game numbers from data/format.json (Comprehensive Rules 1.10.0)

heading: Glossary: keywords and labels
text: Explanations in our own words; the number after each keyword is its rule. Tags in cards.json use the same names (keyword:Blocker, trigger:Deploy ...).

heading: Keyword effects (written as <Keyword>)
text: - Repair n (13-1-1): at the end of your turn this Unit recovers n HP. Several Repair effects add up. - Breach n (13-1-2): when this Unit destroys an enemy Unit with battle damage during your turn, it also deals n damage to the first card of the opponent's shield area (Base first, else the top shield). Adds up. Still works if both Units die; does nothing if the opponent has no Base or shields. - Support n (13-1-3): when you rest this Unit for its Support, another friendly Unit gets +n AP this turn. Adds up. - Blocker (13-1-4): in the block step the defender can rest this Unit to make it the attack's new target. One per attack. - First Strike (13-1-5): when attacking, deals its battle damage first; a target it destroys deals no damage back. - High-Maneuver (13-1-6): while this Unit attacks, enemy Units cannot use Blocker. - Suppression (13-1-7): when its battle damage hits an enemy shield, the next shield takes the same damage at the same time. - Development (13-1-8): part of a timed effect. You may exile the listed number of cards from your trash; if you do, the effect after the ■ happens. Decks with Development want a full trash.

heading: Timing labels (written as 【Label】)
text: - Activate･Main (13-2-1): usable in your main phase while the Unit is not attacking. - Activate･Action (13-2-2): usable in an action step (both players' turns). - Main (13-2-3): Command playable in your main phase when no Unit is attacking. - Action (13-2-4): Command playable in an action step, including during the opponent's battles. - Burst (13-2-5): when this card is destroyed as a shield and revealed, its owner may use the effect for free. - Deploy (13-2-6): triggers when the card is deployed. - Attack (13-2-7): triggers when the Unit declares an attack. - Destroyed (13-2-8): triggers when the Unit or Base is destroyed; works from the trash. - When Paired (13-2-9): triggers when a (qualifying) Pilot is paired with this Unit. - During Pair (13-2-10): applies while a qualifying Pilot is paired. - When Linked (13-2-11): triggers when a Pilot meeting the link condition is paired. - During Link (13-2-12): applies while the link lasts. - Once per Turn (13-2-13): each copy of the card can use this effect once per turn.

heading: Game terms
text: - Active / rested: standing / turned sideways. Rested Units can be attacked; resting is how attacks, blocks and costs are paid. - Trash: discard pile (public). Removal area: where exiled cards go (public). - Field: the resource area, battle area and shield area together (4-1-1-2). - Standby player: the player whose turn it is not. - Link Unit: a Unit paired with a Pilot that meets its link condition; can attack the turn it is deployed.

heading: Action tags used by tools (pattern-based, not official terms)
text: draw, destroy, bounce (return to owner's hand), rest-enemy, set-active, recover-hp, damage, ap-up, hp-up, ap-down, search-deck, add-to-hand, discard, exile, from-trash, token, shield, resource, deploy-other, pair-link, cant-attack-block, self-mill. A tag means the phrase appears in the effect text; always confirm with fetch_card.py before relying on it.

heading: Deck construction and game setup
text: Notes written in our own words. Rule numbers point to the official document; read it for exact wording.

heading: Deck construction (6-1)
text: - Two decks: a main deck of exactly 50 cards and a resource deck of exactly 10 cards (6-1-1). - Main deck: at most 4 copies of any one card number (6-1-1-3). Different art with the same card number counts as the same card. - Resource deck: no copy limit (6-1-1-5). - Colors: the deck is built from one or two colors only (6-1-1-2). - Ban list and restricted list apply on top of these rules at official and sanctioned events. See banlist.md. - Sideboard: the Comprehensive Rules do not define one. The ban list notice mentions "deck and sideboard", so check the BO3 Match Rules page for the event's sideboard policy before you plan side-in / side-out swaps.

heading: Setup (6-2)
text: - Each player shuffles both decks, then draws 5 cards (6-2-1-5). - Redraw (mulligan): optional and only once. Player one decides first. The whole hand goes to the bottom of the deck, the player draws 5 new cards, then shuffles (6-2-1-6, 6-2-1-7). Because the old hand goes to the bottom, the new hand is drawn from the other 45 cards. - Shields: the top 6 cards of the main deck become face-down shields (6-2-2). - Each player starts with an EX Base token (0 AP, 3 HP) in the base section (6-2-3). - Player two starts with one active EX Resource token in the resource area; player one gets none (6-2-4). An EX Resource is removed from the game when it is used to pay a cost.

heading: Winning and losing (1-2)
text: - A player who takes battle damage from a Unit while having no shields (and no Base) loses (1-2-2-1, 8-5-2-2). - A player whose deck is empty at the draw loses immediately (1-2-2-2, 7-3-1-1). Deck-out is a real win route for decks that make the opponent use cards up. - A player may concede at any time (1-2-4).

heading: Limits worth remembering
text: - Hand: discard down to 10 at the end of your turn (7-6-5-1). - Battle area: up to 6 Units. A 7th forces you to trash one of yours; that is not "destroyed" (4-5-4, 11-4-2). - Resource area: up to 15 Resources, of which at most 5 can be EX Resources (4-4-2). - Base section: only one Base. A new Base sends the old one to the trash, which does not count as destroyed (11-5-2).

heading: The five phases (7-1)
text: Start → Draw → Resource → Main → End. The active player drives the turn; the game does not move on while triggered effects are waiting to resolve (7-1-3).

heading: Start phase (7-2)
text: - Active step: all of your rested cards in the battle area, resource area and base section stand up (become active) at once (7-2-3). - Start step: "at the start of the turn" effects resolve (7-2-4).

heading: Draw phase (7-3)
text: Draw 1 card. If the deck is empty after this draw, you lose immediately (7-3-1-1).

heading: Resource phase (7-4)
text: Put the top card of your resource deck into the resource area, face up and active (7-4-1). With a 10-card resource deck this growth stops after 10 turns unless effects add more.

heading: Main phase (7-5)
text: In any order and as often as limits allow (7-5-1): - play a card from hand: deploy a Unit, deploy a Base, pair a Pilot, or use a 【Main】 Command (7-5-2); - use an 【Activate･Main】 effect; - attack with a Unit (see 03-battle.md). You may end the main phase early, which moves straight to the end phase (7-5-5).

heading: Level vs cost (2-9, 2-10, 7-5-2-2)
text: - Lv is a threshold: you meet it if you have at least that many Resources in your resource area, active or rested (2-9-1). Your player level = number of Resources, including EX Resources (2-9-4). - Cost is what you pay: rest that many active Resources (2-10-1). - To play a card you need both: Lv met, and enough active Resources for the cost. A Lv7 / cost 6 card needs 7 Resources on the field and 6 of them untapped. - Tokens count as Lv 0 and cost 0 (2-9-3, 2-10-3). - Practical effect: high-Lv, low-cost cards are "late but cheap" (you can play them alongside other cards once you reach the level); low-Lv, high-cost cards are the reverse.

heading: End phase (7-6)
text: Four steps in order: action → end → hand → cleanup. - Action step: starting with the standby (non-active) player, both players may use 【Action】 Commands and 【Activate･Action】 effects (7-6-3, section 9). - End step: "at the end of the turn" effects resolve. <Repair> heals here (7-6-4, 13-1-1). - Hand step: discard down to 10 (7-6-5). - Cleanup: "during this turn" effects end (7-6-6). Then the turn passes.

heading: Action steps in general (section 9)
text: - Happen after the block step in every battle, and in the end phase (9-1). - The standby player acts first, then players alternate (9-2, 9-4). - Each option: play an 【Action】 Command, use an 【Activate･Action】 effect, or pass (9-3). - The step ends when both players pass in a row (9-5). - A Command with a 【Pilot】 section cannot be paired as a Pilot during an action step (13-2-4-2).

heading: Who can attack, and what (8-1, 3-2-4)
text: - Only Units attack. An active Unit that has not attacked yet may attack in your main phase. - A Unit cannot attack on the turn it was deployed, unless an effect says so. Exception: a Link Unit can attack the turn it is deployed (3-2-6-3). - Targets: the opposing player, or an enemy Unit that is rested. You cannot attack an active (standing) enemy Unit.

heading: Battle steps (8-2 to 8-6)
text: 1. Attack step: rest your Unit and declare the target. 【Attack】 and "when this Unit attacks" effects trigger (8-2-2). 2. Block step: the defender may use one active <Blocker> Unit to redirect the attack to it; that Unit is rested (8-3, 13-1-4). Only one Blocker per attack, and the original target cannot block for itself. <High-Maneuver> on the attacker stops Blockers (13-1-6). 3. Action step: both players may use 【Action】 cards and 【Activate･Action】 effects, defender first (8-4, section 9). 4. Damage step (8-5). 5. Battle end step: "during this battle" effects end (8-6). If the attacker or target leaves the battle early, the battle skips to the battle end step (8-2-4, 8-3-5, 8-4-2).

heading: Damage when attacking the player (8-5-2)
text: - If the defender has a Base, the damage goes to the Base. A Base at 0 HP is destroyed (8-5-2-4). The starting EX Base has 3 HP, so it soaks the first hits. - With no Base but with shields, the damage goes to the top shield. Any damage destroys a shield (each has 1 HP). The shield is revealed; if it has 【Burst】, its owner may use it for free before it goes to the trash (8-5-2-3, 13-2-5). - With no Base and no shields, the Unit's AP is dealt to the player as battle damage, and that player loses (8-5-2-2). - Extra damage does not carry over to the next shield (5-5-6). <Suppression> and <Breach> are the ways to hit more than one card in the shield area (13-1-7, 13-1-2).

heading: Damage between Units (8-5-3)
text: - Both deal damage equal to their AP at the same time. A Unit at 0 HP is destroyed and goes to its owner's trash. - <First Strike> on the attacker: it deals its damage first; if that destroys the target, the target deals none back (13-1-5). - Recovering HP (<Repair>, "recover-hp" effects) only matters if damage persists on Units between battles; confirm the exact damage-persistence rule in section 5-5 / 11 of the official document before relying on it.

heading: Bases (3-5, 11-5)
text: - While a Base is in play, attacks on the player hit the Base first (3-5-3). - Only one Base at a time. Deploying a new Base trashes the old one without it counting as destroyed (11-5-2), so 【Destroyed】 does not trigger.

heading: Practical notes for analysis
text: - Resting is a cost: a Unit that attacked or blocked stays rested until your next start phase, which makes it a legal target for enemy attacks. Effects that rest enemy Units ("rest-enemy" tag) therefore open them to attack. - Effects that set your Units active again ("set-active" tag) let them attack twice or stay ready to block. - Shields protect against lethal but feed the opponent free Burst effects; counting the opponent's Burst cards matters when racing.

heading: Units (3-2)
text: Deployed to the battle area (max 6). The only attackers. Have AP and HP. Most have a link condition (a Pilot name in [brackets] or a trait in (parentheses)).

heading: Pilots (3-3)
text: - Paired by placing them under one of your Units; a Pilot only exists in the battle area while paired (3-3-1, 3-3-3). - One Pilot per Unit. A Pilot cannot be removed or swapped freely (3-3-4, 3-3-5). - The Unit gets the Pilot's AP/HP modifiers while paired (3-3-8-1), and the effect text printed below the Pilot's name (3-3-9). The text above the name, usually a 【Burst】, belongs to the Pilot card itself (it matters when the card is a shield). - The Unit does not gain the Pilot's traits (3-3-7). - If the Unit leaves the battle area, the Pilot goes with it to the same place (3-3-6).

heading: Commands (3-4)
text: - Played for their effect at 【Main】 timing (your main phase) or 【Action】 timing (action steps), then usually go to the trash (3-4-4). - Some Commands also have a 【Pilot】 section and can be paired as a Pilot instead, but not during an action step (3-4-6-2, 13-2-4-2).

heading: Bases (3-5)
text: Go into the base section of the shield area, one at a time; they have AP and HP and absorb attacks aimed at the player. See 03-battle.md.

heading: Resources (3-6)
text: Come from the 10-card resource deck, one per turn, face up and active. They meet Lv and pay costs. Max 15 in the area (5 of them EX).

heading: Tokens (5-17)
text: Created from outside the game as Units, Bases or Resources. No color, Lv 0, cost 0. A token that would move anywhere except the battle, resource or shield area is removed from the game (5-17-2-5). EX Base and EX Resource are tokens.

heading: Pairing (5-9, 7-5-2)
text: Pairing a Pilot from hand is a main-phase action that costs its cost (and needs its Lv). 【When Paired】 triggers when this happens; 【During Pair】 applies while any qualifying Pilot is paired.

heading: Links (2-12, 3-2-6)
text: - A Unit is a Link Unit while a Pilot that meets its link condition is paired with it (3-2-6-2). - A bracketed name such as [Amuro] is met by any Pilot whose card name contains that text (3-2-6-4). - Link Units can attack the turn they are deployed (3-2-6-3). This is the main reason link pairs are strong: deploy + pair + attack in one turn. - 【When Linked】 triggers when the link is made; 【During Link】 applies while it lasts. - For deck building: count how many Pilots in the deck satisfy each Unit's link condition (deck_stats.py "Link coverage").

heading: Effect types (10-1)
text: - Constant: always on while the card is in a place where it works. - Triggered: happens automatically when its condition occurs (e.g. 【Deploy】, 【Attack】, 【Destroyed】). Several matching events at once trigger it only once. - Activated: a player chooses to use it by paying the cost before the colon (【Activate･Main】, 【Activate･Action】). - Command: the effect of a Command card when played. - Substitution: "do B instead of A".

heading: Rules for reading effects
text: - "You may" = optional. Everything else is done as far as possible (10-1). - Effects on Units and Bases work only while those cards are in the battle area or shield area, unless the text says otherwise (10-1-2). 【Destroyed】 is the main exception: it works from the trash (13-2-8). - Targets are chosen when the instruction is reached. If a required target cannot be chosen, that effect does not happen. - "Can't" beats "can": a prohibition overrides an effect that allows the action.

heading: Resolution order
text: - The active player's triggered effects resolve first, then the standby player's. - If several of your own trigger at once, you choose the order. - 【Burst】 effects resolve before all other triggered effects (10-1-6-8). - A new trigger that happens during resolution is resolved first (it jumps the queue).

heading: Activating an effect (10-3)
text: Check conditions → declare (reveal the card if it comes from hand) → resolve → handle anything triggered by it.

heading: Analysis tips
text: - When judging a card, ask which effect type each part is: constant effects are always "on" value; triggered ones depend on how often the trigger happens; activated ones depend on having the cost available. - 【Once per Turn】 limits each card's own copy of the effect, so two copies of the same card can each use theirs (13-2-13).
